label: near and far, and how far away something is
note: Chapter 81. The old note stated the problem exactly: ivide and avide give a two-way here/there and no way to say that something is FAR, so distance could be pointed at and not measured. The chapter separates the two jobs and says so on the page -- the deictic pair POINTS (my side or not my side, and something avide may be a step away or a country away) while aduthu and akale MEASURE. ethra dooram? then asks for a number. One of the four atoms cost nothing: ethra was already inside the age question the learner knows whole, doing exactly this job, and the chapter lifts it out rather than teaching it fresh -- which is a habit the lesson names, because a long sentence learned whole usually holds two or three words that work on their own. The chapter also asks the learner to REFUSE a pattern: akale opens with a and the deictic distal prefix is a-, but the a in akale is part of the word. The test given is whether the other members of the set exist -- there is no ikale and no ekale, so there is no set and no pattern. Verified before writing: aduthu, akale and dooram all returned ZERO files.
